Prevention: Control established populations near waterways to prevent spread during flooding and storm events
Clean equipment and farm machinery after working in an infested area to prevent seeds and stolons being spread; especially important if you do not already have the weed in the area
Rotate crop every year with upland crops such as oil seed crop, legume and maize etc.
Fallow the land for about one season crop (4 months).
Make sure that the field dries out and if the weed is found use direct control methods.
Do not let the weed set seed.
Monitoring: A fleshy, tufted, annual or perennial aquatic herb (10-50 cm high) with a glabrous, shiny appearance and a short rhizome.
It forms rosettes and spreads by short stolons.
Flowers in spikes (3-6 cm long), each with six violet or lilac tepals (the outer parts of the flower) which are spreading at flowering and later spirally contorted
Inspect fields weekly or fortnightly and implement direct control when seedlings or larger plants are found
Direct Control: The weed is not difficult to remove by hand, but requires persistence to remove successive flushes of germination
Regular hoeing and hand weed is required
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
